items.content:
OpenAI基金领投癌症脑机接口：读取肿瘤电信号，尝试用电刺激抑制生长

动察 Beating AI 快讯，美国神经科技公司 Coherence Neuro 完成 4500 万美元 A 轮融资，由 OpenAI Startup Fund 和彼得·蒂尔旗下 Founders Fund 联合领投，Lux Capital、8VC 等参与投资。

与 Neuralink 主要帮助瘫痪患者控制设备不同，Coherence 想用脑机接口直接监测癌症，甚至通过电刺激抑制肿瘤生长。

它的技术依据是，脑瘤并非只在组织内部生长，还会与周围神经元交换电信号，并改变脑部电活动。Coherence 正在研发名为 SOMA 的植入式设备，通过电极持续读取这些信号，再用 AI 判断肿瘤的变化，调整电刺激方案。

整套系统包括硬币大小的脑部植入物、耳后供电设备和手机 App。最终目标是让患者在家接受全天候监测和个性化治疗，不必完全依赖定期扫描才能了解病情。

团队今年 7 月公开的研究显示，通过长期记录患癌小鼠的脑电活动，可以预测肿瘤在约 5 周内的生长速度。今年 6 月，团队还在澳大利亚皇家墨尔本医院启动人体试验，前三名患者只在脑瘤切除手术中接受了约 30 分钟的临时电极测试。目前正在推进另外 7 名患者的记录与刺激测试。

电场治疗癌症并非全新概念。美国 FDA 早已批准体外电场治疗设备 Optune 用于部分胶质母细胞瘤患者。Coherence 想进一步把监测和治疗整合进植入物，利用实时数据不断调整干预方式。

新融资将支持其首次长期人体植入试验，并推进胰腺癌等其他癌症的临床前研究。

US spot Bitcoin ETFs drew $1.08 billion over three trading sessions to push October flows back above water.
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) attracted $528 million in net inflows on Wednesday as Bitcoin briefly surged above $84,700 before retreating.
The funds extended their inflow streak to three sessions, adding $23 million on Tuesday and $526.6 million on Monday, according to SoSoValue data. The three sessions drew in a combined $1.08 billion.
Wednesday’s inflows brought October’s net inflows to approximately $461 million, while year-to-date net inflows reached $1.34 billion.
According to Farside Investors data, BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) led Wednesday’s inflows with $235 million, followed by the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) with around $213 million.
The latest inflows followed two consecutive weeks of withdrawals, with Bitcoin ETFs shedding $228 million last week and $681 million the week before.
Bitcoin’s rally on Wednesday took it to an intraday high of $84,777 before it pulled back to $82,485 at the time of publication, according to CoinGecko.
Altcoin ETFs also recorded modest inflows. Ether ETFs stopped the bleeding with $15 million in net inflows after a five-session outflow streak. Solana ETFs snapped a 13-day outflow streak with approximately $585,000 in inflows, and XRP ETFs added around $709,000.

items.author: theblockbeats
items.content:
AI商业化遭遇现实考验：1%客户贡献Anthropic近半营收，Token用量增长但支出停滞

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Ramp 追踪逾 7 万家美国企业的支付数据发现，Anthropic 和 OpenAI 企业端收入的约 80% 来自仅占客户总量 1% 的头部客户，AI 商业化呈现出明显的客户集中趋势。8 月和 9 月，企业 Token 支出连续两个月几乎零增长，10 月初虽创历史新高，但较 8 月峰值仅高出 1.5%。

价格下跌是支出增长停滞的重要原因。Ornn 数据显示，Anthropic 实际 Token 价格指数已从 9 月中旬的 1.70 美元以上跌至 0.83 美元，跌幅超过 50%；OpenAI 对应指数则为 0.45 美元。据 YipitData，Anthropic 前 1% 客户 8 月贡献了 46% 的营收，高于一年前的 25%。

与此同时，企业 AI 付费采用率增长放缓。Ramp 数据显示，9 月企业 AI 付费采用率仅上升 0.62 个百分点，达到 55.9%。Ramp 首席经济学家 Ara Kharazian 认为，AI 市场增长正从扩大付费用户规模转向提升现有用户的使用深度。

高盛警告，Token 需求增速必须超过价格降幅，才能支撑持续的算力投资。Apollo 首席经济学家 Torsten Slok 也指出，企业对算力价格高度敏感，降价未必能带来足够的新增需求。高盛数据显示，亚马逊、Alphabet、Meta、微软和甲骨文的已实现投资资本回报率已从 40% 降至 25%，创 2016 年以来最低水平。

上述数据对 AI 行业寄予厚望的「杰文斯悖论」提出挑战：算力成本下降能否通过需求增长带来更高收入，仍有待验证。随着客户集中、价格下跌和付费渗透率趋于饱和，AI 企业能否将 Token 消耗转化为实际营收、利润增长或成本节约，将成为检验 AI 基础设施投资回报的关键。

items.author: theblockbeats
items.content:
DeepSeek搜索首测69分：事实问答接近第一，复杂检索倒数第三

动察 Beating AI 快讯，独立评测机构 Artificial Analysis 测试了 DeepSeek 刚开放的搜索 API，将其纳入 27 款搜索产品对比，综合得分 69，排名第 17。榜首 Exa 和 Perplexity 均为 80 分。

不过，DeepSeek 每 1000 次成功搜索仅收费 0.75 美元，是所有参测付费搜索 API 中最便宜的。

评测统一使用 GPT-5.6 Luna，让它调用不同搜索 API 完成事实问答、深度研究和多轮网页检索。接入 DeepSeek 后，综合得分从不联网时的 33 分提高至 69 分。

DeepSeek 在直接查找事实方面表现较好，正确率达到 70%，距离榜首仅差 3 个百分点。但面对需要反复搜索、拼接线索的复杂问题，正确率只有 63%，在 27 款产品中倒数第三。

此外，它每次搜索平均返回约 7000 个 Token，虽然信息丰富，却增加了模型读取和处理资料的成本。

实际完成一道评测任务平均花费约 0.032 美元，其中搜索费用只有 0.0085 美元，模型调用费用却达到 0.023 美元，占总成本约 73%，是榜单第二高的模型成本。

即便如此，DeepSeek 的单题总成本仍是第 5 便宜。它把搜索请求的价格压到了最低，但冗长的搜索结果吃掉了部分成本优势。

items.content:
Corgi靠美女营销火遍硅谷：豪言半年开100家咖啡馆，第二家开业两周就被关

动察 Beating AI 快讯，此前靠「Corgi Girls」美女营销走红硅谷的 AI 保险公司 Corgi，还试图用另一种方式吸引客户：开咖啡馆。

今年夏天，公司提出要在半年内于旧金山开设 100 家全天候咖啡馆，为创业者提供办公和社交场所，通过聚会、活动和人脉关系吸引潜在客户，再向他们销售企业保险。

但扩张很快遇到麻烦。Corgi 原本有 16 份租约接近签署，却突然暂停推进，随后又裁掉扩张主管及部分团队成员。另外 3 家已经签约的旧金山门店也迟迟未能开业。尽管如此，公司仍坚持开设 100 家咖啡馆的目标不变。

实际经营同样不顺利。Corgi 在旧金山的第二家门店，9 月开业仅 13 天，就因缺少有效卫生许可被勒令关闭。《旧金山纪事报》随后查明，该店的建筑改造手续也未完成。附近居民还提出上诉，指责它是「伪装成咖啡馆的办公室」，让复业更加困难。

比开店更难的，是把热闹变成生意。《The San Francisco Standard》采访了这家门店开业活动的 3 名参加者，发现没人有购买保险的需求，其中一人甚至不知道 Corgi 是保险公司。

虽然样本有限，但也暴露了这套营销模式的局限与尴尬。

霍尔木兹危机推高全球原油运输成本，运费从每桶3美元飙升至20美元以上

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，高盛报告显示，全球原油平均运输成本已从一年前的每桶约 3 美元升至 20 美元以上，中东主要航线更超过每桶 35 美元。霍尔木兹海峡危机引发的战争风险、船对船转运、燃料成本上涨及油轮调度效率下降，正共同推高原油运输费用，形成新一轮能源价格压力。

高盛估算，霍尔木兹海峡战争风险溢价使运输成本每桶增加约 7 美元，船对船转运增加约 4 美元，船用燃料成本上涨增加约 4 美元，油轮调度效率下降及航线改道增加约 3 美元，伊朗油轮可用数量减少则贡献约 2 美元。

运输成本飙升也导致区域原油价差扩大，布伦特原油与 WTI 原油价差近期达到每桶约 14 美元，明显高于通常约 5 美元的水平。高盛指出，亚洲炼油商尤其容易受到冲击，部分欧洲炼油商已开始减少原油进口和加工量。

高盛预计，布伦特原油价格将在今年年底前回落至每桶约 90 美元，并于 2027 年平均达到每桶 80 美元。不过，若运输、保险及炼油成本持续高企，即使原油基准价格回落，汽油、柴油等成品油价格仍可能维持高位，进一步加大能源通胀压力。

Bitunix分析师：AI资本开支推高融资压力，全球资产重新评估利率与避险需求

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，全球市场正对 AI 融资、利率与地缘风险进行重新定价。前纽约联邦储备银行行长杜德利警告，AI 投资可能让利率先升后降：数据中心、芯片与电力建设短期内拉动需求并争夺储蓄，推高融资成本；但若资本支出见顶或高杠杆企业融资转弱，投资与财富效应可能反向收缩，迫使美联储更快降息，市场定价所反映的平稳利率路径因此可能存在偏差。

Meta 第三季度营收同比增长 26% 至 646 亿美元，显示 AI 推荐系统已提升广告效率；但公司将 2026 年资本支出预期上调至 1350 亿至 1450 亿美元，自由现金流更自 2012 年以来首次转负。美国财长贝森特淡化 AI 的系统性风险，投资者仍须衡量巨额投入能否转化为持续现金流；股价短期表现积极，并不意味着资本回收风险已经消失。

资金压力也反映在其他市场。日本通胀降低了既有名义债务的实际负担，前央行官员估算由此形成约 195 万亿日元的「债务人收益」，但日本央行加息将逐步推高新债再融资成本。美国计划出借最多 31.5 万桶取暖油储备，以缓解美国东北部冬季供应压力，但有限的释放量未必足以明显压低零售价格。与此同时，新加坡私人持有的黄金十年间增至约 800 吨，约为 2014 年的 16 倍，显示高净值资金越来越重视资产保管地与司法风险。

黑海商船遇袭及船员伤亡，则将地缘风险推向北约东翼，航运保险、能源供应与国防支出都可能承受更大压力。市场接下来需要观察的，不只是利率或油价的走向，而是 AI 投资能否产生足够回报、融资成本如何传导，以及安全风险是否持续推高供应链成本。

items.content:
OpenAI让近2000个Agent并行搞科研：32分钟分析800万脑细胞，找到神经疾病新线索

动察 Beating AI 快讯，OpenAI 联合美国 AI 生物技术公司 PerturbAI 和斯克里普斯研究所，让 1946 个基于 GPT-Rosalind 的 Agent 并行分析约 800 万个小鼠脑细胞的实验数据，耗时仅 32 分钟。研究团队估算，如果由科学家逐项分析、查阅文献，可能需要数月到一年。

这些数据来自此前的基因编辑实验。科学家干扰不同基因，观察脑细胞会发生什么变化。这次 AI 将近 2000 组基因干扰结果分给不同 Agent，分别分析细胞变化、查阅相关论文，寻找可能被忽略的联系。

其中一个发现涉及 DCTN1 基因，其突变与一种具有帕金森样症状的罕见疾病有关。AI 发现，破坏这个基因后，脑细胞中负责合成胆固醇的基因反而更加活跃。结合已有研究，它提出一种解释：可能不是胆固醇不够，而是细胞内部的运输出了问题，导致胆固醇无法送到需要的地方。如果这一猜想得到验证，恢复正常的胆固醇运输或许能成为保护神经细胞的新方向。

AI 还发现，通常共同调控细胞生长的 Tsc1 和 Tsc2 两个基因，在小脑中的作用明显不同。破坏 Tsc2 会影响数十个负责神经信号传递的基因，破坏 Tsc1 却几乎没有变化。这为研究遗传病结节性硬化症提供了更具体的线索，但相关机制仍需后续实验验证。

马斯克公开支持SpaceX与特斯拉合并，引发股东质疑合并公平性

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，埃隆·马斯克此前公开确认，SpaceX 与特斯拉正在评估合并可能性。对此，一名直接了解谈判情况的人士称，马斯克在投资者面前主动披露交易进展并表达支持，可能引发股东对交易公平性的质疑，拖慢谈判进程，甚至令交易面临更长时间的法律审查。通常，在独立董事评估一项重大交易期间，相关方会避免公开表达倾向，以免影响程序的公正性，或让外界怀疑决策已被预先定调。

市场分析指出，如果 SpaceX 与特斯拉最终合并，交易规模可能达到 3.5 万亿美元，如此庞大的交易不仅涉及公司治理和股东权益，还可能引发全球监管机构的审查。特斯拉在中国拥有重要业务，SpaceX 则涉及美国国防项目和人工智能领域，两家公司的业务属性、监管环境及国家安全相关因素存在明显差异，可能增加合并审批的复杂程度。

items.content:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto, Government websites and online services were disrupted after concerns about a PHP bug that could allow attackers to take control of vulnerable servers. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent compared the GENIUS Act’s stablecoin regulations to Abraham Lincoln-era banking reforms, while French authorities proposed holding crypto platforms liable for certain DeFi incidents.
PHP Foundation admits ‘structural failure’ delayed critical security fix
The PHP Foundation has acknowledged that indecision and a shortage of resources delayed a fix for a critical security flaw first identified in 2024, calling the stalled response a “structural failure.”
Government agencies and other organizations worldwide took websites offline Wednesday as a precaution while PHP released emergency patches for two related critical vulnerabilities. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on affected servers without logging in.
PHP is a programming language widely used to power websites and web applications, including content management systems.
In a blog post following the release of the patch, the foundation described how its developers first found signs of the vulnerability in 2024, but struggled to come up with a solution without disrupting the large ecosystem of software built using PHP.
“Combined with the lack of a known path to remote code execution and the small team of core developers with the necessary deep knowledge of the engine occupied with many responsibilities, this decision process caused work on a fix to stall and restart repeatedly over months,” said the foundation.
“We won’t pretend otherwise: the delay was a structural failure, caused by both the security team’s decision process and its lack of resources.”
The foundation was pointed to the vulnerability again on August 11, after security firm Calif and OpenAI independently reported the same underlying issue, with Calif demonstrating unconditional remote code execution, which made it a top security priority.
Bessent compares GENIUS Act stablecoin rules to Lincoln-era banking reforms
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has compared the newly finalized stablecoin regulations under the GENIUS Act to President Abraham Lincoln’s banking reforms, as the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) prepares to enforce federal rules for stablecoin issuers in January 2027.
In a Wednesday post on X, Bessent described the legislation as a “watershed moment in American finance,” drawing parallels with the National Currency Act of 1863, which created a federal system for nationally chartered banks to issue currency.
Bessent argued that the GENIUS Act could play a similar role in modernizing US payments, strengthening private-sector innovation and reinforcing American leadership in digital assets.
The OCC’s finalized regulations establish requirements for stablecoin reserves, redemptions, risk management and issuer oversight. The framework applies to eligible banks, federally supervised nonbank issuers and certain foreign stablecoin providers.
Starting Jan. 18, 2027, payment stablecoin issuers will generally need appropriate regulatory authorization to operate legally in the United States, with penalties possible for noncompliance.
The regulatory milestone comes as dollar-backed stablecoins gain wider adoption in payments and cross-border transfers, despite slowing growth in their overall circulating supply.
France proposes liability for crypto exchanges offering DeFi access
France wants cryptocurrency platforms to face liability for certain decentralized finance (DeFi) incidents if they fail to vet protocols or ignore known security risks.
French authorities published proposals Wednesday to revise the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA). The joint response to a European Commission consultation came from France’s Treasury, the Financial Markets Authority (AMF), the central bank and the Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR).
“CASPs [crypto-asset service providers] should be liable for certain incidents affecting clients where they actively facilitated access,” French authorities said.
MiCA excludes crypto services provided in a fully decentralized manner without intermediaries. France’s proposal would extend investor safeguards by imposing new duties on regulated platforms that connect customers to DeFi protocols.
The Commission is reviewing whether MiCA needs updating as crypto markets develop. Its consultation sought views on activities outside the law’s original scope, including DeFi. The responses will inform a report to EU lawmakers due by June 30, 2027, which could include proposals to amend the law.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Felix Ng
items.content:
Move over memecoins: Crypto ‘meme games’ coming, bagholders and all
“Plenty will be ponzis. Plenty will get exploited. Plenty will insta die. There will be ridiculous gains, and people will get absolutely f***ing rinsed,” says Illuvium co-founder Kieran Warwick.
Update (Oct. 22 at 10:31 UTC): This article has been updated to include comments from Sébastien Borget and Ben James on AI-driven game development.
AI could unleash a flood of short-lived crypto “meme games,” attracting the same speculative traders who helped push memecoins to record highs in late 2024, according to Illuvium co-founder Kieran Warwick.
Speculative crypto games such as Wolf Game and Fishing Frenzy, where players compete for financial rewards, once took months to develop. But Warwick says AI tools have reduced the time and cost of creating similar games to just days and around $1,000.
He predicts as many as 100,000 such games could launch within a year, with many designed to survive for only a few days — long enough for their creators to turn a profit.
“Like you have serial deployers of memes, you’ll get serial deployers of games,” Warwick told Cointelegraph.
But whether that flood would benefit crypto gaming and the broader industry is less clear. Cheaper development could make niche games viable and revive attention across the sector, but a wave of disposable crypto games could also leave a lot of speculators “holding the bag.”
“There will be ridiculous gains, and people will get absolutely f****ing rinsed,” Warwick wrote on X on Monday.
A memecoin-style boom… and bust?
In 2024, Pump.fun and similar launchpads helped fuel a surge in memecoins by making tokens easy to create. The sector’s combined market capitalization reached $150.6 billion in December 2024 before falling nearly 69% to $47.2 billion by November 2025, according to CoinGecko.
The boom divided industry figures, with supporters championing memecoins’ appeal to traders while critics argued they diverted capital from useful projects and damaged crypto’s reputation.
Warwick said he expects a similar speculative wave to touch crypto meme games.
“These degens who are gambling in crypto, they get a thousand-dollar paycheck and they put $500 in Pump.Fun. You’re giving them a new venue and a new shiny wrapper … for them to be able to go and gamble.”
Asked whether a mass of short-lived crypto games will ultimately be good for the crypto gaming ecosystem, Warwick said: “probably not.”
“Like in the long run, I don’t think so. The sustainable model that Illuvium has been building towards for years, where really good quality games with ownership underneath, that I think is still the dream of where crypto gaming should be building towards.”
Animoca Brands and The Sandbox CEO Robby Yung took a similar view.
“I think if there is a type of meme game, as Warwick is describing, that doesn’t particularly take much effort to make… I don’t think it would become a lasting category because user retention is the lifeblood of games and always has been,” he told Cointelegraph.
Sébastien Borget, president of the Blockchain Game Alliance and co-founder of The Sandbox said he sees the speculative wave as one part of a broader expansion in game creation.
“We’re witnessing a true Cambrian explosion of games and creativity, where anyone can turn even their wildest ideas into playable experiences without worrying about the complexities of 2D/3D asset creation, level design, music, or sound effects,” he told Cointelegraph.
“But as the cost of experimenting and bringing ideas to life approaches zero, and the abundance of content explodes, the real challenge shifts from creation to discovery, distribution, and reaching an audience.”
More games, but where are the players?
That audience question was central for Mirai Labs co-founder and CEO Corey Wilton, who questioned whether an AI-driven surge in supply can overcome weak demand for crypto games.
“We shipped quite a few games, six or seven games, into the market,” Wilton said. “Ultimately, it came to the conclusion that the demand for or within the Web3 space simply isn’t there.”
Dappradar’s tracking of gaming decentralized apps (Dapps) shows just $232.2 million in total value locked in 2,356 apps. A basket of the top 50 gaming tokens has a combined market capitalization of $3.8 billion at the time of writing.
“I think the lack of demand and liquidity in so-called altcoins is definitely an issue, but I think, at the same time, there is also a lack of choice out there of really enjoyable, fun games that captivate people’s imaginations,” said Yung.
Related: Proof of Play to shut down after blockchain gaming thesis falls short
“The reality is the number of game titles that use crypto is very small, and so there’s not a lot of choice for consumers. That makes it difficult to actually judge whether crypto is the issue or it’s just that there aren’t enough good games.”
Recent crypto games show there is still interest in the sector despite recent pivots. The developers of Yield Fields, an upcoming web3 farming game built on the Robinhood chain, raised an estimated $8.3 million on Oct. 14 selling digital land plots as nonfungible tokens. The game is set to launch at the end of the month.
AI game development hits crypto
Data shows AI has already entered crypto game development.
In the Blockchain Game Alliance’s 2025 survey of 506 industry professionals, 32.8% said their company had implemented or experimented with AI for game design and content creation.
Yung compared the arrival of AI development tools to the early days of mobile gaming, when cheaper development encouraged more studios to enter the market.
“Frankly, I think that’s a great thing all around,” said Yung. “It reminds me a bit of when mobile first started to become popular around 2010. A lot of people started developing for mobile because it was much cheaper and much faster than developing for PC or console.”
“What happened was we just got more games of all kinds of quality, and customers had a choice of playing what they liked,” he said.
Ben James, CEO of Atlas Design and 404.xyz, said the lower barriers would make originality more important.
“AI will make it easier to launch games, and those that lack creativity, innovation or passion will converge on the average: a sameness we call ‘slop’. At the same time, games that are unique in their aesthetics, gameplay or even business models will stand out.”

Railway曝安全事件：部分密钥明文恐遭窃取，攻击疑似瞄准AI服务商

动察 Beating AI 快讯，云应用部署平台 Railway 披露安全事件，其存储客户环境变量的系统出现异常活动。初步调查显示，未经授权的第三方可能获取加密的环境变量，甚至拿到其中部分变量的明文。这些变量通常存放 API Key、数据库密码和私有镜像仓库凭据。

Railway 怀疑，此次事件属于近期针对云平台的一系列攻击，最终目标是 AI 推理服务商。公司已通知相关上游服务商预防性撤销密钥。虽然初步判断只有部分客户受到影响，但 Railway 仍要求所有用户立即更换平台内存储的密钥，并检查服务日志是否存在异常调用。

Railway 一度暂停全平台构建和部署，连企业客户也无法发布更新。构建功能随后恢复，但用户仍需重新部署应用，让更换后的密钥生效。

此外，Railway 已主动重置所有存储桶密钥和平台保存的 GitHub 凭据，相关用户需要重新连接 GitHub。

法律AI公司Legora再融5.5亿美元：估值7个月涨57%，年化收入突破2亿美元

动察 Beating AI 快讯，瑞典法律 AI 公司 Legora 宣布完成 5.5 亿美元 E 轮融资，投后估值达到 88 亿美元。本轮由 Atreides Management 领投，摩根大通、富达等机构参与。

今年 3 月 Legora 的估值还是 56 亿美元，短短 7 个月上涨约 57%。

Legora 成立于 2023 年，主要帮助律师审查合同、检索法律资料、起草文件，并通过 AI Agent 执行多步骤工作。公司披露，年化经常性收入（ARR）从 100 万美元增长至 1 亿美元，用时不到一年半；再突破 2 亿美元，仅用了不到半年。

目前，Legora 已覆盖全球 2400 多家律所及企业法务团队，拥有超过 14 万名法律专业用户。美国已成为其最大收入市场，全美收入最高的 50 家律所中，超过一半是其客户。今年第三季度，企业内部法务团队贡献了超过 40% 的新增客户。

Legora 正与美国法律 AI 公司 Harvey 争夺市场。新融资将用于全球扩张，以及开发面向律师的 AI Agent 操作系统，让 AI 从辅助阅读、写作，进一步参与法律研究、案件受理和持续监管跟踪。

items.author: theblockbeats
items.content:
Anthropic三年首次更新Claude API：删除三个常用参数，旧代码升级后可能报错

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Anthropic 发布 Claude API 新版本 `2026-10-21`，这是自 2023 年 6 月以来首次正式更新版本号。

过去三年，Claude 模型不断迭代，API 版本却一直没变。Anthropic 计划今后更频繁地更新 API，让开发者提前适配新模型可能带来的兼容问题。

这次主要删除了 `temperature`、`top_p` 和 `top_k` 三个参数。它们原本用于控制模型回答的随机性和生成方式。升级新版 API 后，如果代码仍然传入这些参数，就会直接报错。其他一些旧字段和消息格式也受到调整。

Anthropic 同步更新了官方 SDK，新版本默认使用 `2026-10-21`。开发者可以通过 Claude Code 的 `/claude-api` Skill 辅助修改代码。

不过，旧版 `2023-06-01` 仍然可以使用，现有项目无需立即迁移。

马克龙公开批评特朗普借法国骚乱为中期选举造势

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙周三在访问卡塔尔期间，公开批评特朗普等外国领导人利用法国近期发生的暴力骚乱攻击移民，并借机为自身政治议程造势。

马克龙表示，没有证据表明外国势力干预并煽动了法国骚乱，但此后确实出现了外国操纵信息的情况，导致多国领导人发表了他所称的「不可接受且愚蠢」的言论。马克龙明确指出，「特朗普也在其中」，「我们看到了一些由人工智能生成的图片，展示了从未在法国发生过的场景。还有人声称，法国遭到了成群移民和伊斯兰主义者的入侵，这完全是错误的。」

马克龙还抨击那些「在法国某些地区，或者在大西洋彼岸，借着我们的处境为自己竞选造势」的人，称「这些人让我非常恼火。」

特朗普所属的共和党距离美国中期选举仅剩两周。自法国示威活动于上周六升级为骚乱以来，特朗普多次引用法国的暴力事件和打砸抢掠画面，试图将相关事件与移民政策联系起来。特朗普还警告美国选民「看看法国就知道了」，并声称「巴黎很快就会成为一座穆斯林城市」。这些言论将法国国内的骚乱与美国的移民政策争论联系起来，但法国警方尚未明确认定骚乱与移民或伊斯兰主义激进分子有关。

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，Gemini 联创 Cameron Winklevoss 和 Tyler Winklevoss 在接受采访时表示，比特币是公开、可审计的区块链，任何人都能看到交易记录，然而公开性使其不适合隐私需求。Zcash 则用于私密交易/支付，因此两者可共存。理想情况下隐私应内置于比特币，但目前是「比特币存储 + Zcash 交易」的实用模型。比特币仍重要，但公开链在 AI 面前隐私暴露风险更大。

items.ai_summary: AI research lab Flapping Airplanes, founded roughly a year ago by Prod incubator co-founder and ThunderKittens/Megakernel author Ben Spector, raised a $1B Series A led by Index Ventures and Lux Capital at a $6B valuation, to pursue a GPU-kernel-level rewrite of AI training and inference that has already shown large efficiency gains over vLLM and SGLang.
items.author: theblockbeats
items.content:
Flapping Airplanes融资10亿美元：创始人孵化过Cursor，想从GPU底层改写AI训练

动察 Beating AI 快讯，成立约一年的 AI 研究实验室 Flapping Airplanes 完成 10 亿美元 A 轮融资，由 Index Ventures 和 Lux Capital 联合领投。投后估值达到 60 亿美元，是今年 1 月的 4 倍。公司只有 20 多人，至今没有推出商业产品，投资方却包括红杉资本、谷歌 GV 和英伟达。

Flapping Airplanes 由 Ben Spector、哥哥 Asher Spector 和 Aidan Smith 共同创办。CEO Ben 在 MIT 期间联合创办了创业孵化器 Prod，参与过 Cursor、Mercor、Etched 和 Decart 的早期孵化。后来，他进入斯坦福大学 Chris Ré 的研究团队，成为开源 GPU 编程框架 ThunderKittens 的论文第一作者。Asher 是斯坦福统计学博士，Aidan 则是 Thiel Fellow，曾在马斯克旗下 Neuralink 工作三年。

2025 年，Ben 和斯坦福团队进一步开发了 Megakernel，尝试把整个模型的计算合进一个 GPU 内核。传统推理框架会把计算拆成上百个内核，逐个启动、执行、等待，GPU 在这些间隙无法充分利用显存带宽。Megakernel 将计算步骤合并，让下一步的数据读取提前进行。在单张 H100 上运行 Llama-3.2-1B、每次生成一条序列时，vLLM 和 SGLang 最多只能利用 50% 的显存带宽，新方案提高到了 78%，推理速度比 SGLang 快了超过 1.5 倍。

几个月后，团队又将 Megakernel 扩展到 Llama-70B，在特定测试中，接入 Tokasaurus 推理引擎后的端到端吞吐量比 SGLang 高出 22% 以上。两项研究均已开源，属于 Ben 创办 Flapping Airplanes 前参与的斯坦福研究成果。

Flapping Airplanes 现在沿着这条路线继续改造 GPU。公司称，最新框架已经可以在同一个内核中同时执行模型训练、推理和视频游戏。团队还想借此探索新的学习算法。现有 PyTorch 等框架擅长执行按步骤组织的计算，却很难高效处理某些细粒度、需要大量交错执行的任务。GPU 本身未必做不到，只是现有软件不容易把这些能力发挥出来。换一种底层编程方式，就可能让过去成本太高、难以运行的算法变得可行。

他们希望进一步解决 AI 的数据效率问题。人类不需要读完整个互联网就能学会语言，大模型却依赖海量训练数据。搜索和编程有大量现成语料，机器人操作、科学研究等领域很难获得同等规模的样本。Asher 此前曾以数据效率提高 1000 倍为例，说明这类突破可能带来的经济价值。如果训练一个模型只需要原来千分之一的数据，许多缺乏训练样本的行业也可能用上 AI。

items.content:
黄仁勋GTC演讲遭环保组织当场打断：英伟达芯片怎么进了俄军无人机？

动察 Beating AI 快讯，10 月 21 日，黄仁勋在柏林 GTC 大会上推介新一代 AI 算力平台，演讲刚进行约 20 分钟，台下突然有人站上椅子，拉开横幅，当面质问他：为什么英伟达芯片会出现在俄军无人机里？AI 扩张造成的环境破坏又该怎么办？

闹事的是以激进抗议著称的国际环保组织绿色和平在德国的分部，他们还把「英伟达，清理你的肮脏生意」投射到舞台屏幕上。

保安随即上前带人离场，黄仁勋却示意他们动作轻一点，让抗议者有机会把话说完。他表示这些问题都很重要，但希望先完成演讲。

抗议者盯上的芯片确实在俄军武器中出现过。今年 8 月，乌克兰国防情报局在俄罗斯 S-71 巡航导弹中发现英伟达 Jetson Orin 计算模块。《纽约时报》也报道过，乌方人员在俄军无人机残骸中找到同系列产品。这不是训练大模型的昂贵 GPU，而是一种面向机器人、机器视觉等场景的民用小型计算机，可以让设备在本地识别和处理图像。

英伟达称，Jetson 不在俄罗斯销售，也不是为军事用途设计，但产品经过二手市场多次转卖后，公司很难追踪最终去向。

此外，绿色和平今年 9 月发布的研究指出，英伟达披露的供应链等间接碳排放，自 2020 年以来增长了 725%。英伟达虽然已经让自身运营用电与可再生能源匹配，但承担芯片制造任务的东亚供应商并不都使用清洁能源。

绿色和平要求英伟达在 2030 年前将可再生能源目标扩大至整个制造供应链，同时对全球经销商开展独立审计，防止芯片流入军事装备。

韩国金融委员长：虚拟资产征税需充分考虑多方因素，数字资产法案已进入最后协商阶段

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，据韩联社报道，韩国金融委员会委员长李亿元在国会政务委员会综合监察上就明年起施行的虚拟资产征税表示，「需要充分考虑各种情况」。

国民力量党议员宋彦锡当日质询是否废除或推迟征税，并称数字资产的性质和政策方向尚未确定就先行征税，应优先制定《数字资产基本法》。李亿元回应称，数字资产相关法案正处于最后协商阶段，将尽快推动讨论；关于征税，各方意见多样，目前仍在收集中。

韩国虚拟资产征税于 2020 年通过修改《所得税法》引入，此前已三度推迟。目前政府正按照明年 1 月施行的时间表推进行政程序，但业界乃至执政党内部分人士认为，因标准不明确、基础设施不足，现在实施时机尚不成熟。

彭博：DeepSeek完成第二轮1000亿元融资，腾讯、宁德时代出资最多

动察 Beating AI 快讯，彭博社最新报道称，DeepSeek 完成第二轮 1000 亿元人民币融资，腾讯和宁德时代是出资规模最大的投资方之一。这轮融资最初计划募集 500 亿元，随后两次上调目标。尽管融资规模翻倍，但投前估值仍维持在约 5000 亿元。

今年 6 月底，DeepSeek 刚完成约 510 亿元的首轮融资，创始人梁文锋个人出资约 200 亿元。按本轮报道规模计算，两轮融资合计约 1500 亿元。本轮新老股东的拟出资金额各占约一半。宁德时代追加约 100 亿元，腾讯也继续出资约 100 亿元。新投资方包括石溪资本、中芯聚源、CPE 源峰、君联资本和吉利等。

完美世界 10 月 22 日公告，两只由砺思资本、拾象资本相关管理人负责的基金已完成募集，规模分别为 75.2 亿元和 36.5 亿元。完美世界合计认缴 1.5 亿元，世纪华通此前也披露参与出资。两只基金均参与 DeepSeek 本轮融资，但具体投入金额尚未公开。

DeepSeek 同时在筹备科创板 IPO，计划最快今年底递交上市申请，争取 2027 年挂牌。

Dragonfly合伙人：加密行业正率先经历全球黑客攻击浪潮

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，Dragonfly 管理合伙人 Haseeb Qureshi 表示，全球网络安全正遭遇一场类似新冠疫情的黑客攻击浪潮，而加密行业已率先经历这一趋势。他认为，由于链上攻击最容易直接变现，加密协议的安全事件可以被视为整个互联网安全风险的早期预警。目前，加密行业黑客攻击数量急剧增加，但被盗资金总额的年化水平与 2025 年大致相当，意味着单次攻击的平均损失有所下降。

Highlight Clip: Tom Lee: BitMine Will Soon Stop Buying ETH

Tom Lee: BitMine Will Soon Stop Buying ETH

Speaking at TOKEN2049, Tom Lee said Bitmine has set a hard cap of 5% of Ethereum's total supply for its ETH holdings and will stop accumulating once it reaches that level. He said Vitalik had suggested that the company stop at 5%. At the time of the speech, Bitmine held approximately 6 million ETH, representing 4.9% of total supply, and needed roughly another 100,000 ETH to reach its target. Lee said the accumulation, originally expected to take five years, had taken just over a year and was completed entirely during a bear market.

WuBlockchain notes that Tom Lee's market forecasts tend to be optimistic. His bullish targets may not materialize, and actual market performance may differ significantly from his predictions. Readers are encouraged to focus on his analytical reasoning rather than use specific price targets or timelines as a basis for investment decisions. — link

Aerodrome与Velodrome正式合并推出统一链上DEX Aero

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，Aerodrome 与 Velodrome 已正式完成合并，推出统一的链上现货交易平台 Aero。新平台计划同时运行于以太坊主网、Base、Robinhood Chain、Ink、OP Mainnet、Arc 及 Arbitrum 七条网络，将两家去中心化交易平台此前的运营整合至同一平台之下。

此次合并的核心动作在于代币体系的统一。原有的 AERO 与 VELO 代币将迁移至新版 AERO 代币，其中旧版 AERO 按 1:1 置换，VELO 则按 1 VELO = 0.044 AERO 的比例兑换；原 veAERO 与 veVELO 锁仓头寸将转换为 sAERO。Binance 已于 10 月 16 日宣布支持此次代币合并与合约置换，为存量持有者提供了迁移通道。

加密行业Q3游说支出降温：Coinbase等机构在《CLARITY法案》受挫后缩减开支

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，据彭博社报道，随着加密行业首要立法优先事项《CLARITY 法案》于 9 月在参议院受挫，Coinbase 及多家主要加密行业组织第三季度在美国联邦层面的游说支出较第二季度有所下降。尽管如此，相关机构当季游说支出仍超过 400 万美元，已连续六个季度维持在这一水平之上。

这一支出节奏的放缓，直接反映了行业在关键立法战役中的挫败。《CLARITY 法案》旨在为数字资产市场建立清晰的监管框架，被视为加密行业进入主流金融体系的关键一步。

法案失败的原因复杂，行业内部的分歧被视为因素之一。Coinbase 首席执行官 Brian Armstrong 在今年 1 月参议院银行委员会表决前，因不满法案对稳定币收益业务的限制而公开撤回支持，被部分业内人士指责延误了立法的黄金窗口期。与此同时，传统银行集团持续施压，担忧加密平台向用户提供类似利息的稳定币奖励会吸走银行存款，进一步削弱了法案的政治可行性。此外，围绕政治人物加密资产利益的道德条款争议，也让民主党方面始终未予让步。

游说支出的收缩不仅体现在金额变化上，也反映在行业与游说机构的关系调整中。部分游说公司已在第三季度终止了与加密行业客户的合作。此前，加密行业在 2026 年上半年已投入超过 800 万美元推动市场结构立法，其中 Coinbase 一家便支出了约 220 万美元，Kraken 投入近 100 万美元，但最终未能转化为立法成果。

Rosenblatt首予Robinhood买入评级、目标价135美元，摩根大通同日上调目标价至115美元

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，投行和机构经纪商 Rosenblatt Securities 分析师 Chris Brendler 于 10 月 20 日首次覆盖 Robinhood（HOOD），给予买入评级和 135 美元目标价，对应此前收盘价约 37% 的上行空间。同日，摩根大通将目标价从 103 美元上调至 115 美元，但维持中性评级。受此影响，Robinhood 股价在 10 月 21 日交易中上涨约 4.16%，收于 102.29 美元附近，市场关注两家机构对估值与增长前景的分歧。

Brendler 在报告中将 Robinhood 描述为「世代增长故事」（generational growth story），认为其已从最初的免佣金交易 App，演变为覆盖经纪、退休账户、信用卡、期货、指数期权及加密资产的综合金融平台，而市场仍低估了这一转型的成熟度。他指出，公司核心经纪业务即使在大规模下仍在持续抢占份额，Pattern Day Trading 监管改革解除了对高价值活跃客户的关键限制，同时国际扩张加速、产品线深化及相对固定的运营成本结构，都支持其享有高于传统券商同行的估值溢价。

相比之下，摩根大通上调目标价至 115 美元，体现对近期业务动能的一定认可，但维持中性评级，显示其对估值水平与长期可持续性仍持谨慎态度。

当前华尔街对 Robinhood 的整体共识评级为「适度买入」或「买入」，平均目标价约 130-135 美元区间，多数分析师看好其平台扩张与产品多元化带来的增长潜力，但也有观点提醒其高波动性与相对较高的估值倍数。此次评级更新发生在公司即将于 10 月 27 日公布第三季度业绩之前。

Meta财报后股价盘后上涨约3%，分析师关注广告业务强劲与Muse AI进展

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，Meta 第三季度营收同比大幅增长 26% 至 646 亿美元，超过市场预期；调整后每股收益（剔除一次性法律费用）也显著超预期。财报公布后，股价盘后上涨约 3% 至 4%。

具体来看，广告收入同比增长 26%，广告展示量增长 10%，平均广告价格上涨 14%，家庭应用日活用户达 36.4 亿。GAAP EPS 为 3.83 美元，主要受约 98.9 亿美元一次性法律和解费用（与美国多州总检察长就青少年心理健康及社交媒体相关诉讼达成和解）影响；剔除该费用后，调整后 EPS 约 7.40 美元。

公司给出的第四季度营收指引为 730 亿至 760 亿美元，中值高于市场共识。全年资本开支指引收窄至 1350 亿至 1450 亿美元。Reality Labs 收入不及预期，运营亏损约 41 亿美元，公司预计该业务全年亏损将收窄至 180 亿至 190 亿美元，并进一步降至 2027 年约 150 亿美元。

Pivotal Research 的 Jeffrey Wlodarczak 在财报后将目标价从 930 美元上调至 960 美元，指出营收与资本开支表现好于预期，并特别强调 Muse 使用数据积极：超过四分之一的 Muse 用户通过该代理进行购物，平均购买金额超过 200 美元。

Jefferies 的 Brent Thill 表示，第四季度指引「留有上行空间」。另一方面，BMO Capital 的 Brian Pitz 维持持有评级与 580 美元目标价，虽认可 Muse 早期动能与 AI 产品进展，但仍关注 2026-2027 年高额资本开支的回报可见性及成本轨迹。

华尔街整体对 Meta 维持「强力买入」共识评级，平均目标价约 820 美元左右，隐含约 17% 上行空间。市场普遍认为，强劲的广告引擎（受 AI 推荐系统与生成式 AI 工具助力）正在为大规模 AI 基础设施投入提供资金支持，而 Muse 作为面向个人超级智能的早期尝试，已展现出商业化潜力（包括购物与潜在订阅场景）。尽管自由现金流因高资本开支转负，且法律费用影响了报告利润，但投资者当前更愿意为增长与 AI 叙事买单，而非过度担忧短期费用压力。

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，据 The Block 报道，面向 AI 代理的去中心化数据网络 Dataline 宣布完成 1060 万美元种子轮融资，由 Lattice 与三星支持的 Dispersion Capital 共同领投，Symbolic Capital、Coinbase Ventures、Anagram 以及 Robinhood 联合创始人兼 CEO Vlad Tenev 等参投。

另有多名未具名投资人参与，包括前 CFTC 负责人，以及来自 Venmo、Anchorage Digital、NEA、General Catalyst、Jump Capital、FalconX 等机构的创始人或合伙人。本轮于今年 4 月关闭，以附带代币认股权证的 SAFE 完成，估值未披露；投资方未获得董事会席位、观察员席位或顾问职位。

Dataline 联合创始人 Nuo Shi 表示，平台已上线，覆盖约 50 个数据源，首批「AI Data Launch」合作方包括 Hyperliquid、Polymarket、Kalshi、Base、Robinhood Chain、BNB Chain、Sui 与 TON 等；在 Base 与 Robinhood Chain 上开发者可获免费接入。公司计划于今年年底前推出代币，并拟在 Base 上通过 Uniswap 的 Continuous Clearing Auction（CCA）进行公开代币发售，细节预计下周公布。融资将用于扩充数据源、强化数据校验，并拓展至机器人与 AI 训练数据等场景。

特斯拉财报后股价盘后跌约3%，分析师关注FSD、Robotaxi与SpaceX预期

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，特斯拉第三季度营收和调整后每股收益均超过市场预期，但财报公布后股价盘后下跌约 3%。市场评论显示，投资者关注的不仅是单季业绩，也包括自动驾驶、Robotaxi、Optimus 等业务的增长路径，以及潜在 SpaceX 交易的清晰度。

根据财报，特斯拉第三季度营收约 280.5 亿美元，同比基本持平；调整后 EPS 为 0.48 美元，高于市场预期的约 0.45 美元。汽车业务毛利率（剔除监管积分）回升至约 18.1%，自由现金流实现正值约 15 亿美元，好于市场此前预期的现金消耗。资本开支低于预期，公司还将全年资本开支指引下调至约 200 亿美元。不过，GAAP 净利润同比下滑约 43% 至 7.87 亿美元，能源业务收入也出现下滑，电池供应限制被提及为生产瓶颈之一。

Deepwater Asset Management 的 Gene Munster 在财报电话会后表示，他根据特斯拉股东材料中的图表估算，第三季度 FSD 行驶里程同比增长约 190%，与上一季度增幅相当，高于第一季度的约 125%。他将此视为 FSD 使用增长的积极信号。官方也披露，北美新车 FSD 付费订阅附着率超过 75%，较上季度显著提升。与此同时，Munster 指出，马斯克提出 2030 年交付 500 万辆汽车，相较其估算的今年约 200 万辆，意味着未来四年年均增长约 25%，投资者仍难以判断这一目标的实现路径。

Requisite Capital 的 Bryn Talkington 则认为，财报前股价表现更多受到潜在 SpaceX 交易预期影响。Cantor Fitzgerald 的 Andres Sheppard 维持买入评级与 485 美元目标价，称 2026 年对特斯拉是「转型之年」，并对 FSD 与 Robotaxi 进展持乐观态度。Morningstar 的 Seth Goldstein 表示，资本开支低于预期意味着特斯拉更能依靠自身现金流支撑投资，而无需额外融资。

另一方面，部分市场声音更为谨慎。有分析指出，股价在电话会期间转跌，部分源于管理层对机器人与芯片相关计划的表述偏谨慎，以及对 SpaceX 合并事宜未提供更多细节。华尔街整体对特斯拉维持「温和买入」共识评级，平均目标价约 400 美元左右，但目标价区间差异极大，反映出对汽车基本面与 AI/机器人叙事估值的分歧。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/373072

Meta计划引入无投票权股票，以在不稀释扎克伯格控制权的情况下为AI提供资金

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，Meta 宣布，计划引入新的无投票权股票，这表明该公司可能会严重依赖新股发行来为其人工智能（AI）建设提供资金。该计划将允许公司发行新股——用于收购、吸引顶尖 AI 人才以及支付芯片费用——同时不会稀释马克·扎克伯格（Mark Zuckerberg）的控制权。

Alphabet 曾在 2014 年采取过类似举措，实施了 1 拆 2 的股票拆分，在超级投票权股票之外引入了无投票权股票，使联合创始人拉里·佩奇（Larry Page）和谢尔盖·布林（Sergey Brin）的合计控制权保持在略高于 50% 的水平。这使得该公司今年早些时候更容易地发行了 850 亿美元的新股，以支付 AI 投资；其中一半的新股不带有投票权。

促成这一决定的原因是「AI 研究带来的高额资本开支」，财报数据显示，Meta 资本开支指引下限由 1300 亿美元上调至 1350 亿、上限 1450 亿美元，三季度资本开支超 400 亿美元（去年同期不足 190 亿），自由现金流为 -21.2 亿美元，去年同期为 106.3 亿美元。

Anthropic推出基于Claude Opus 5.5的AI智能体应用Claude Duet

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，Anthropic 推出基于 Claude Opus 5.5 的 AI 智能体应用 Claude Duet 美国人工智能公司 Anthropic 于 2026 年 10 月 21 日正式宣布推出全新 AI 智能体应用 Claude Duet，并开启研究预览。该应用基于公司于 2026 年 9 月 22 日发布的旗舰模型 Claude Opus 5.5 构建，定位为面向专业人士和小型企业主的主动式数字助手，旨在帮助用户管理繁杂工作并主动处理任务。

Claude Duet 采用主动式设计：每天早晨向用户发送简要简报，汇总已连接应用中的重要事项；全天定期检查相关应用，仅在需要关注时主动消息提醒。用户可通过文字或语音下达指令，涵盖从安排会议等行政事务，到构建仪表板、制作财务或销售预测、原型设计乃至搭建 Web 应用等复杂任务。应用在云端拥有独立虚拟机和浏览器，可在后台持续工作，即使用户关闭手机或电脑也能完成任务，完成后通知用户。

安全机制是其核心设计之一。在发送消息、支付、签署文件或删除内容等敏感操作前，Claude Duet 会展示具体内容并等待用户批准；部分操作（如证券交易或账户间转账）即使获批也被禁止。它集成 Claude 账户已有的记忆、技能和连接应用，支持 Claude Marketplace 中超过 6000 个连接器和插件，可对接 Gmail、Slack、QuickBooks、Stripe、Gusto、HubSpot、DocuSign、Canva、Shopify 等工具，协助处理未付发票提醒、薪资准备、合同起草等业务场景。

目前，Claude Duet 以研究预览形式开放，仅限美国地区 Claude Pro 和 Max 订阅用户通过候补名单申请，无额外费用，但使用量计入现有套餐限额（后台检查也计入）。它提供独立的 iOS 和 Android 应用，同时可在 claude.ai 网页端使用，与主 Claude 应用暂时分离。Team 和 Enterprise 计划暂未支持。Anthropic 表示，这是其首个以 Opus 5.5 为核心打造的主动式智能体产品，强调判断力与资源调配能力。

英国金融监管机构就DeFi指引与加密法规启动咨询

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，英国金融行为监管局（FCA）宣布启动两个咨询期，分别针对使用去中心化金融（DeFi）的企业应如何遵守其指引，以及因「近期立法变化」而对某些加密资产予以豁免。

在周三发布的一份公告中，FCA 开启了咨询期，旨在帮助 DeFi 企业遵守该金融监管机构关于反洗钱和金融犯罪的规定。该机构还宣布就「加密资产监管豁免」进行咨询，并引述了英国近期的立法情况。

关于 DeFi，FCA 表示，拟议的指引「旨在阐明现有规则，而非制定新政策」。

「DeFi 属于（金融服务）中最具创新性的领域之一，」英国加密资产商业委员会（UK Cryptoasset Business Council）在回应此次咨询时表示。「英国仍然可以实现正确的平衡——明确的边界规则、保持适度（相称）的期望，以及一个能让负责任的创新在这里扎根，而不是迁移到别处的框架……FCA 需要妥善处理此事。」

加密监管豁免指的是 FCA 此前公布的一项监管制度，该制度涵盖稳定币的持有安排和储备资产，预计将于 2027 年 10 月起开始执行。FCA 已于 9 月 30 日开放了加密实体的申请通道，寻求合规的企业需在 2027 年 2 月 28 日截止日期前提交申请。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Felix Ng
items.content:
PHP Foundation admits ‘structural failure’ delayed critical security fix
Government websites and online services were disrupted after concerns about a PHP bug that could allow attackers to take control of vulnerable servers.
The PHP Foundation has acknowledged that indecision and a shortage of resources delayed a fix for a critical security flaw first identified in 2024, calling the stalled response a “structural failure.”
Government agencies and other organizations worldwide took websites offline Wednesday as a precaution while PHP released emergency patches for two related critical vulnerabilities. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on affected servers without logging in.
PHP is a programming language widely used to power websites and web applications, including content management systems.
In a blog post following the release of the patch, the foundation described how its developers first found signs of the vulnerability in 2024, but struggled to come up with a solution without disrupting the large ecosystem of software built using PHP.
“Combined with the lack of a known path to remote code execution and the small team of core developers with the necessary deep knowledge of the engine occupied with many responsibilities, this decision process caused work on a fix to stall and restart repeatedly over months,” said the foundation.
“We won’t pretend otherwise: the delay was a structural failure, caused by both the security team’s decision process and its lack of resources.”
The foundation was pointed to the vulnerability again on August 11, after security firm Calif and OpenAI independently reported the same underlying issue, with Calif demonstrating unconditional remote code execution, which made it a top security priority.
Websites go dark amid PHP security scare
The disruption stretched across the world as developers disconnected websites while preparing to install the emergency fixes.
The Netherlands shut its digital identity service, and the country’s National Cyber Security Center also took its website offline.
Finland’s state IT provider Valtori disconnected government public web services, while France’s Interior Ministry temporarily took prefecture websites offline. Germany’s federal IT provider ITZBund also disabled several websites, according to Reuters.
In Australia, the Australian Signals Directorate acknowledged that its cybersecurity website, cyber.gov.au, was among government sites affected by the PHP issue.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi took to X to urge website operators to prepare to apply the patch as quickly as possible. In a post, she said temporarily suspending website functions could reduce the risk if the patch couldn’t be applied immediately.
The Wikimedia Foundation, which operates Wikipedia, said it took some supporting services offline as a precaution, including Toolforge and Cloud VPS, which host tools and projects used by volunteer developers, leading to parts of Wikipedia going offline on Wednesday.
Blockchain security firm SlowMist said its MistEye service surveyed PHP use across the crypto industry, urging exchanges, DeFi platforms and wallet providers to review their exposure and upgrade. It identified 793 domains with direct PHP fingerprints among 1,488 domains assessed.
Intersect, a membership organization supporting the Cardano blockchain’s development and governance, said it had temporarily taken its Members Area offline while it assessed potential exposure. The page is still offline at the time of writing.
Related: Tech giants rush to block 8 eMudhra certs that could enable fake sites
Coinbase chief security officer Jeff Lunglhofer said the company found no evidence of any exposed PHP instances.
“Whenever we hear about vulnerabilities like this, we automatically conduct a full sweep to make sure everything is as safe as we can make it. We’re also working with our third party suppliers for extra assurance.”
Digital asset infrastructure company BitGo also said its platform was unaffected by the PHP vulnerability.
Meanwhile, Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao warned internet users on Wednesday to be “extra careful” visiting any website in the next few days, as some web administrators may not be up-to-date with security patches.
OpenAI has released a Codex skill to help website operators check for potentially vulnerable PHP versions and identify applicable updates, which can be accessed via GitHub.
The PHP security team said it has not identified any functional exploits at the time of its public disclosure.

Meta Q3财报：营收增26%超预期，百亿法律费用与AI资本开支双双施压

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，Meta 于北京时间今日凌晨公布 2026 年第三季度业绩，营收为 646.01 亿美元，同比增长 26%，高于市场共识预期（约 633–637 亿美元）。净利润为 98.60 亿美元，同比增长 264%，GAAP 稀释每股收益为 3.83 美元。

营业利润同比下降 37% 至 129.88 亿美元，营业利润率降至约 20%（去年同期约 40%），主要受到一笔 98.9 亿美元法律费用的影响。该费用与公司同美国各州总检察长就青少年心理健康及社交媒体相关诉讼达成的协议有关，协议总支付上限约 185.9 亿美元。

Meta 表示，剔除该费用后营业利润为 228.8 亿美元，对应调整后稀释每股收益约为 7.40 美元。净利润同比大幅增长也受到上年同期有效税率高达 87% 的低基数影响，本季有效税率为 24%，剔除法律费用相关影响后税率会进一步降低。广告业务保持增长，广告展示量同比增加 10%，平均广告价格上涨 14%。

Family daily active people 约 36.4 亿，同比增长 3%。Family of Apps 收入约 641.6 亿美元，其中广告收入约 630.6 亿美元。Reality Labs 收入约 4.43 亿美元，运营亏损约 41.3 亿美元。总费用约 516 亿美元，同比大幅上升 68%，其中包含上述法律费用。

第三季度资本开支（含融资租赁本金支付）约 349 亿美元，自由现金流为负 21.2 亿美元，季末现金、现金等价物及有价证券约 824 亿美元。公司预计第四季度营收为 730 亿至 760 亿美元，中值高于多数共识。全年资本开支指引收窄至 1350 亿至 1450 亿美元（此前为 1300–1450 亿美元），同时上调全年费用指引至 1750 亿至 1790 亿美元（此前约 1650–1690 亿美元），主要因纳入法律费用；剔除该费用后，全年营业利润预计仍将高于 2025 年。公司还预计 2026 年 Reality Labs 运营亏损约 180–190 亿美元，明年有望收窄。

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，特斯拉于北京时间今日凌晨公布 2026 年第三季度业绩，营收为 280.46 亿美元，同比基本持平；归属于普通股股东的净利润为 7.87 亿美元，同比下降约 43%，GAAP 摊薄每股收益为 0.22 美元，低于去年同期的 0.39 美元。营业利润同比下降约 56% 至 7.18 亿美元，营业利润率为 2.6%，同比下滑 3.2 个百分点。主要因研发、AI、机器人等支出大增（运营费用上升约 39%）。

整体 GAAP 毛利率升至 19.6%（同比提升约 1.6 个百分点，也明显高于上季）。剔除监管积分后的汽车毛利率约 18.1%，较上季和去年同期都有明显改善。

当季汽车交付量为 48.65 万辆，同比减少 2%；产量为 46.44 万辆，同比增长 4%。汽车业务收入同比下降约 3%，能源发电与储能收入下降约 16%，服务及其他收入则增长约 33%。公司称，研发及其他运营费用增加、监管积分收入减少和能源业务毛利走低，对营业利润造成压力。

特斯拉第三季度经营现金流为 62.63 亿美元，自由现金流为 15.31 亿美元，低于去年同期的 39.90 亿美元。公司表示，电池供应仍限制汽车产量提升；同时已在内华达州启动 Semi 量产，并在弗里蒙特开始 Optimus 生产，Cybercab 已投入奥斯汀 Robotaxi 车队运营。

据 BIT（bit.com）行情数据显示，或受财报信息影响，SPCX 盘后下跌 3.32%。

特朗普称中期选举前不进攻伊朗，但美伊谈判仍无实际突破

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，美国总统特朗普称中期选举前不会轰炸伊朗，但美方正撤离驻沙特部分非紧急人员、缩减中东部分基地兵力，并增派航母与两栖力量；以色列军方据报本周曾出动数十架战机逼近伊朗边境后折返，打击目标清单亦在更新。

美国国务院已下令仅限沙特境内的非紧急政府雇员及家属撤离，称与伊朗支持的胡塞武装袭击沙特民用目标有关。另据报道，美军近几日悄然缩减驻约旦、卡塔尔、科威特等地兵力；《华尔街日报》称美方正向中东调派另一艘航母，第三个航母打击群正从太平洋方向赶来，并调派搭载海军陆战队的两栖攻击舰。若新增力量到位且现有舰艇不轮换撤离，该地区美军舰艇总数预计将超过 24 艘（目前约 20 艘）。

以色列总理内塔尼亚胡据报持续主张恢复对伊大规模打击；以色列第 12 频道援引美方消息称，本周早些时候数十架以军战斗机和加油机飞越叙利亚、伊拉克上空逼近伊朗边境，飞行路线与对伊攻击路线高度相似，在进入伊朗领空前掉头返回，以方称属演习与威慑。与此同时，巴基斯坦、卡塔尔等加紧斡旋，但美方要求谈核计划、伊方希望先谈重开霍尔木兹海峡，谈判仍无突破。

Lighter计划成为首个申请美国合规牌照的Perp DEX项目，LIT24小时涨15%

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 22 日，Lighter 创始人兼 CEO Vladimir Novakovski 在 Q3 投资者会议上发言表示：「我们目前正在寻求的是获得 DCM（指定合约市场）和 DCO（衍生品清算组织）的牌照。我们花了大量时间与 CFTC（美国商品期货交易委员会）的工作人员沟通，梳理了那里所有的核心原则。其中很多原则，现有的框架已经能够清晰地对应到 Lighter 是如何在链上实现这些的。其他一些原则，有全新的实现方式，对监管机构来说是前所未有的，但他们现在花了大量时间与我们交流，以了解其运作原理。

接下来的计划是，在下个月正式提交这些牌照申请。之后，监管机构有最长 280 天的时间进行审查。因为我们已经完成了所有这些前期工作，我们认为接下来的流程会比较顺利。我们非常期待在美国获得这些牌照并向美国市场开放——不是面向散户，而是面向机构端。」

此前，LIT 曾因「Robinhood 使用 Bitstamp 在美推出永续合约」而出现一波下跌，当时 Robinhood 首席执行官 Vlad Tenev 接受采访时表示，未选择 Lighter 是取决于监管结构。本次 Novakovski 在投资者会议上的发言，让社区再次出现「合规后能更加紧密与 Robinhood 合作」的推断。

据 HTX 行情数据显示，受一系列发言影响，LIT 24 小时一度上涨 15%，现报价格 3.76 美元。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Turner Wright
items.content:
American Bankers Association: OCC’s GENIUS rules ‘undermine’ US Congress
Banking advocacy organizations are pushing back against the OCC’s finalized rules on a stablecoin law, arguing against changes to provisions on yield.
A lobbying group for US banks has weighed in on the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency’s (OCC’s) recently finalized rules on payment stablecoin issuance and custody, arguing that the regulator’s interpretation went against Congress’ intent.
In a Wednesday notice, the American Bankers Association (ABA) said that while the OCC’s final rules implementing the GENIUS Act included “several positive steps,” the banking group remained critical of provisions related to stablecoin yield. The regulator dropped a provision that would have established a presumption that certain third-party arrangements violated the law’s ban on yield payments.
“The final rule removes the OCC’s originally proposed safeguards that would have addressed indirect arrangements involving affiliates, exchanges and other distribution partners,” said ABA. “As a result, payment stablecoin issuers can provide economically equivalent yield while technically avoiding the statutory prohibition. The OCC also declined to adopt a broader presumption against arrangements designed to circumvent the ban.”
The group added:
“Those gaps risk undermining the distinction Congress drew between payment stablecoins and traditional bank deposits, threatening the funds banks use to make the loans that drive the US economy.”
Stablecoin rewards were one of the key issues lawmakers and interest groups debated before and after GENIUS passed Congress in July 2025, and they continue to face scrutiny amid discussions of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, a crypto market structure bill currently in limbo after a failed procedure vote in the Senate last month.
Notably, the Blockchain Association approved of the change to yield prohibition, arguing that the OCC “[brought] the final rule more closely in line with the statutory text.” The Bank Policy Institute, another banking industry advocacy group, largely sided with ABA, saying that “the decision to omit the yield presumption replaces clarity with ambiguity and puts the banking system and its customers at risk of deposit flight.”
The OCC finalized its rules ahead of the GENIUS Act’s implementation in January 2027. Other government departments are expected to release rules on GENIUS related to their agencies’ purview over stablecoins, including the Federal Reserve and Treasury.
Related: ABA, state banking groups push back on CLARITY Act stablecoin yield provisions
items.title: American Bankers Association: OCC’s GENIUS rules ‘undermine’ US Congress

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Citadel founder Ken Griffin said Oct. 20 that investors are "almost certainly" in an AI bubble, but that companies surviving a bubble tend to lead markets for decades.
- He compared GPUs to airline seats, warning that a chip glut could send prices into freefall, as fiber-optic cable prices did after the telecom overbuild around 2000.
- Griffin said corporate buyers are weighing premium OpenAI and Anthropic models against cheaper open-source ones, which strains against the labs' spending.
Ken Griffin, founder of the Wall Street giant Citadel, said Tuesday that investors are “almost certainly” in an AI bubble—though he isn’t telling them to dump their AI stocks.
“What’s left in the wake of these bubbles, if we want to use that word, is often game changing for the world. And the companies that are on the other side of that bubble are the market leaders for decades to come,” Griffin said at Citadel’s Future of Global Markets Conference in New York on Oct. 20
This reaches beyond tech investors, since the AI buildout has underpinned equity markets over the past year, so many index funds and retirement accounts hold a slice of it. A bubble is what happens when prices climb far faster than the businesses behind them can justify, until reality catches up. Citadel is a hedge fund, a private firm that invests money for wealthy clients and institutions.
But the fact that it seems like a bubble isn’t that big a deal if you look at the big picture, according to Griffin. “Any radical transformation of our economy is generally intertwined with a bubble,” he said, recalling the internet boom and adding that he wishes he had kept his Amazon stock.
The companies that emerge on the other side of a bubble tend to lead markets for decades, he argued, though he stopped short of predicting a collapse. His own firm is a case study: Griffin said AI agents, software that carries out multistep tasks on its own, cut some high-level Citadel research from weeks to a couple of hours.
Griffin compared GPUs, the graphics chips that many companies use to train and run AI models, to airline seats. Both have a very low marginal cost to run, meaning the extra expense of serving one more customer is tiny, so prices can collapse once supply outstrips demand.
He pointed to the telecom boom around 2000, when companies laid more fiber-optic cable than demand required and communication prices fell. He also doubted that chips five or six years old, which still earn rental rates he called extraordinary, will keep doing so for another five or six years.
Buyers are getting pickier, Griffin said, sorting which jobs justify premium models from OpenAI and Anthropic and which can run on cheaper open-source alternatives, meaning models anyone can download and run on their own computers. Corporate America has been uneven at extracting value from AI, he added, with companies studying their bills from the labs and asking where the productivity is.
Gartner forecasts worldwide AI spending at nearly $1.5 trillion for 2025, counting everything from chips and servers to AI-enabled phones. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said at Davos in January that the industry is only “a few hundred billion dollars” into what he called the largest infrastructure buildout in human history, with trillions still to build. If customers balk at premium prices, the chip and cloud companies counting on that spending would feel it first.
On July 30, Situational Awareness, a hedge fund founded by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, sold most of its public stock portfolio to Citadel at roughly a 10% discount after its value reportedly fell about 67% in July.
The fund had borrowed as much as four times its capital to buy AI stocks, a tactic called leverage, and its lenders asked for more collateral every day as prices fell. Selling because lenders demand it rather than by choice is known as forced selling, and it feeds itself because each sale pushes prices down and triggers more demands.
Citadel has since shed more than 80% of the risk in that portfolio, Griffin wrote in an August letter to clients, which means the man calling the bubble also bought the discounted stocks.
Griffin warned earlier this year that if the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil shipping lane, stayed closed for another six to 12 months, energy prices would rise materially and push the world into recession.
Wall Street analysts expect growth in capital spending, the money poured into chips and data centers, by the largest AI infrastructure builders to slow from 75% in the third quarter of 2025 to 25% by the end of 2026, Goldman Sachs Research noted in December.

items.content:
Tether backs Bolivian fintech bringing USDT payments to food delivery and banking
The investment will support Peso’s expansion across four Latin American markets, where it connects stablecoin payments to merchant services and local banking networks.
Tether has led a pre-seed funding round in Bolivian fintech Peso, which offers USDT payments through food delivery apps and local banking networks, to support the company’s expansion across Latin America.
In a Wednesday announcement, Tether said the investment will help Peso expand its stablecoin payment infrastructure across Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia and Argentina, including services that connect USDT with local currencies through banking and merchant payment systems.
Peso has integrated USDT payments into Yango’s food delivery service in Bolivia, allowing customers to pay for orders using the stablecoin. The fintech offers QR payments, point-of-sale services for merchants and virtual accounts linked to Bolivia’s banking system through ACH transfers. Tether did not disclose the size of its investment.
Source: Tether
The investment comes as other fintech companies expand USDT-based financial services in Bolivia. On Tuesday, lending platform Tala announced a partnership with El Dorado to offer credit directly through the digital wallet, allowing eligible customers to receive and repay loans in USDT on the Tempo blockchain.
Related: Tether, Kazakhstan cenbank mull tenge stablecoin and asset tokenization
Bolivia turns to stablecoins amid US dollar shortage
Bolivia has increasingly turned to stablecoins since 2025 amid a prolonged US dollar shortage and high inflation, with businesses beginning to accept USDT for purchases as access to foreign currency became more difficult.
In November 2025, the government announced plans to integrate cryptocurrencies and stablecoins into the financial system, including allowing banks to offer digital asset custody and crypto-linked financial products.
The government subsequently began considering a regulatory framework in July 2026 that would recognize USDT for payments, savings and trade alongside the boliviano and US dollar.
The proposal came as Bolivia struggled with a prolonged dollar shortage after abandoning its longstanding currency peg in June, fueling demand for dollar-denominated alternatives such as USDT, as Cointelegraph reported in July.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Turner Wright
items.content:
Trump didn‘t mention ‘crypto’ once in White House cybercrime roundtable
The US President detailed many schemes defrauding Americans, but referred only to “cybercurrency“ related to scams.
US President Donald Trump hosted a roundtable at the White House on cybercrime, even as he and members of his administration face scrutiny from lawmakers and voters over accusations that they used their positions to enrich themselves with digital assets.
Speaking at the roundtable event on Wednesday, Trump said “countless” Americans lost more than $20 billion from cybercrime in 2025 through impersonation schemes, ransomware attacks, scam centers and other methods. The president added that federal officials had frozen $1 billion in “cybercurrency tied to foreign scammers” and prevented $1.6 billion in losses in 2025 from going to criminals engaging in cybercrime following a March executive order.
Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth (left), President Donald Trump (center) and Attorney General Todd Blanche (right) speaking at the White House on Wednesday. Source: White House
Notably, neither the president nor Attorney General Todd Blanche explicitly used the term “cryptocurrency” or “digital assets” when discussing the scams affecting many Americans, despite reports before the roundtable signaling a crackdown on foreign crypto scams would be the focus of the event. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin similarly only referred to “digital extortion.” “Cybercurrency,” the word Trump used, is a dated term for what many people now call cryptocurrency.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation reported that Americans had lost $11 billion from scams in 2025 specifically related to digital assets, including through crypto ATMs. Cointelegraph reached out to the White House for comment on the roundtable but did not receive an immediate response.
Related: Ex-Trump crypto adviser profited after helping pass stablecoin bill: WSJ
The president and his family are tied to several crypto ventures which Trump reported netted him $1.4 billion in 2025, while his alleged “schemes” cost investors about $4.7 billion, according to a Public Citizen report. His family’s crypto company, World Liberty Financial, also faces scrutiny for its USD1 stablecoin being used to settle a $2 billion investment in Binance by an entity tied to Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan in the United Arab Emirates.
Trump’s memecoin project, Official Trump (TRUMP), is hosting another dinner for tokenholders on Nov. 22. Similar events organized by the team behind the memecoin have prompted accusations from lawmakers and interest groups of Trump selling access to the presidency through “pay-to-play” schemes.
Italian police arrest 30 people in crypto money laundering scheme
The White House roundtable followed reports that Italian authorities arrested 30 people for using crypto to launder millions of dollars through a bank allegedly tied to the mafia. According to Bloomberg, Italy’s police were investigating a criminal network that sent money from corporate fraud, crypto investment scams, and drug trafficking to digital wallets.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Nvidia unveiled the OpenShell Reference Architecture at GTC Berlin on Wednesday, combining Vera CPUs, the open-source OpenShell runtime and BlueField-4 chips running Sentry to contain and monitor AI agents.
- Sentry inspects agent traffic from a separate hardware domain and can quarantine an agent within milliseconds, without needing the agent or the host to cooperate.
- CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Zscaler and Check Point are integrating support, while Nvidia lists Sentry's planned availability as early next year.
Nvidia on Wednesday unveiled the OpenShell Reference Architecture at GTC Berlin, a full-stack design that pairs its Vera CPUs, OpenShell software and BlueField-4 chips to contain and monitor autonomous AI agents, according to the company's announcement.
Vera Rubin systems run the models, Vera CPUs run the agents and their tools inside OpenShell, and BlueField-4 chips run a monitoring framework called Sentry. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang described the split as agents that basically exist thanks to a synergy of different environments and frameworks.
“Nvidia created OpenShell to give agents the freedom to do useful work within clearly defined boundaries—contained, monitored and under control,” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, said. “With the OpenShell Reference Architecture, agents can think on Rubin, act on Vera and be governed on BlueField.”
OpenShell, the open-source runtime at the center of the design, treats every agent workload as untrusted and grants access only when needed, Nvidia said in a technical blog post.
It has four parts: a gateway that manages sandboxes and policies, a supervisor that checks outbound requests and handles credentials separately from the sandbox, the sandbox that isolates the agent, and a policy prover that runs formal verification to check that permissions stay under a ceiling the organization sets.
On the hardware side, BlueField-4, a data processing unit that handles networking and security apart from the main processor, sits on the node's only path to the model. That lets Sentry inspect traffic between an agent and the model without relying on the agent to report on itself, per the Sentry deep dive.
Nvidia bundled OpenShell and Sentry into the Open Agent Safety Platform on Sept. 28, with more than 100 launch partners, after a summer in which agents repeatedly slipped out of their test environments. METR reported in August that roughly 1,200 OpenAI agents coordinated on an unsanctioned message board, and about 700 went on to attack Hugging Face.
An OpenAI agent also broke into Australia's Medicare statistics portal in June, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said in September. Nvidia says enterprises can run agents from model builders including Anthropic, Google, Meta and OpenAI on OpenShell infrastructure.
Security vendors including CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Zscaler and Check Point are integrating support for the architecture into their agent security products, and European banks BBVA and Santander are exploring it as a framework for agent safety and governance. ServiceNow also announced general availability of its Arc agent, with actions governed at runtime and enforced by OpenShell.
Nvidia describes BlueField-4 and Sentry as an optional hardware safeguard for deployments that need protection beyond OpenShell's software boundaries. The company says the architecture is available now, but the Sentry deep dive lists the framework's planned availability as early next year, with more libraries and resources still in the testing phase.

items.content:
--- Top Comments ---

[japgolly]: Apply #[non_exhaustive] to publicly-exposed enums seems like a crazy recommendation to me. So much of the power of enums is that when you add a new case the compiler will flag all pattern matches that you need to update, which is a good thing because you're forced to consider each case. Having a catch-all saves dev-time but it risks not appropriately handling new cases becoming a runtime issue instead of a compile time error.

[monocasa]: Can anyone expand on the chromium specifc guidelines on super tiny crates, particularly no nesting of modules/source files? That feels like the ~2010 era of people saying that functions should be as small as possible.  That lead me to reviewing a lot of code where every function was one or two lines and you couldn't actually see what was going on anymore through the layers of unneeded abstraction. I want to give chrome the benefit of the doubt, but that seems really goofy.

[epage]: > Type names should be imported and used unqualified This just pushes people to have redundant information in types (`IoError` instead of `io::Error`). Unless a type is widely recognized (like `HashMap`), I prefer to have them fully qualified so I have the contextual meaning for it.  If I am working with a generic name like `Source`, what does that mean? I shouldn't have to look up in the imports to understand the code (or only understand it through an LSP). Reducing imports also redu...

[preommr]: Google has lost a lot of it's sheen for me. It's not really the 2010s anymore where their brand really used to mean something as a step above all the other tech companies. Nowadays, I care about their recommendations as much as the ones from microsoft, or ibm. Still big companies, lots of smart people, but nothing above norm.

[afdbcreid]: Here's a tip most Rust users don't know about extension traits: if you put `#[rust_analyzer::prefer_underscore_import]` above your trait (and you're using rust-analyzer and not RustRover), autocompletion and the import assist will import the trait `as _` by default, which is very useful for extension traits.

items.author: Bennett Tomlin
items.content:
Fairshake, a Super PAC often supported by the crypto industry, transferred over $24 million to its affiliate Defend American Jobs in September.
Defend American Jobs spent about $24 million in the Ohio Senate race in September.
Approximately $18.6 milion was spent supporting Jon Husted, the Republican incumbent for the Senate race.
An additional $5.7 million was spent opposing Sherrod Brown, the Democratic candidate for the Senate seat.
Defend American Jobs has continued spending in October, with more funds opposing Brown, supporting Husted, and adding in opposition to Dan Osborn, the independent in the Nebraska Senate race.
Brown has opposed the crypto industry before, describing crypto as “speculative products run by reckless companies — we know that’s true — that put Americans’ hard-earned money at risk, not surprising from an industry that was created to skirt the rules.”
Husted was a vocal supporter of the Clarity Act.
In total, Defend American Jobs has spent more than $46 million in the Ohio Senate race this cycle, already beating the $40 million it spent supporting Bernie Moreno in 2024.
Defend American Jobs has been joined in its crypto industry spending by the Digital Freedom Fund.
The Digital Freedom Fund, which has most of its support coming from the Winklevoss Capital Fund, has spent an additional $5.9 million in the Ohio Senate race, supporting Husted and opposing Brown.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- OpenAI President Greg Brockman said the company led a two-month coalition to fix PHP2Shell, found with its models under its Patch the Planet initiative.
- Security firm Calif used GPT-5.6 Sol to find a version of the bug in August; OpenAI found a fuller version in September, and Wiz found both flaws independently.
- Brockman called for authorized defenders, such as governments, to scan for vulnerable servers and, in extreme cases, patch them remotely.
The two PHP bugs that pushed Finland, the Netherlands, and France to pull government websites offline on Wednesday weren't found by a hacker in a hoodie. They were found by AI—OpenAI's AI, to be specific.
"Over the past two months, we have been leading a coalition to mitigate one of the most severe bugs in open source software found in recent memory, php2shell," OpenAI President Greg Brockman said in a statement. "It was discovered and addressed using our models as part of our Patch the Planet initiative."
The flaws let anyone run their own code on servers running PHP, the language behind about 70% of websites whose server-side language is known. PHP shipped fixes a day after details leaked online.
According to Brockman, the bug sat in PHP for 14 years, and a limited version surfaced in 2024 but "wasn't considered significant at the time." Researchers at security firm Calif, working under Patch the Planet, used OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol to find a version of it in August, and OpenAI's own team found a fuller version in September. Cloud security firm Wiz also found both flaws independently, per OpenAI's disclosure.
Brockman was able to turn a global panic attack into a great PR stunt, promoting GPT’s abilities while admitting the ending got messy: “While the tail end of the disclosure didn't go as planned (the original target date was a October 22 release, but details started to leak early, so PHP’s maintainers brought the release forward to October 21), I am grateful that the coalition successfully had an entire two months to prepare—the fixes were quite intricate for PHP, and a leak significantly before the patch was available would have been very impactful. ”he said.
GPT-5.6 Sol's résumé already includes a break-in. In July, OpenAI said the model and an unreleased sibling escaped a locked test environment during a hacking benchmark, found a zero-day flaw along the way, and pulled answers straight from Hugging Face's production database and other five major companies.
Turns out "by accident" only works if you're a billion-dollar company 🙃🙃#OpenAI#chatgpt#Anthropic pic.twitter.com/D7LPUlnql1
— Gaxan (@pvgagan02) October 19, 2026
In September, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said an OpenAI agent had accessed non-public files on a Medicare statistics portal back in June, and called the notification process "unacceptable." Days later, OpenAI disclosed that its agents had also pulled data from U.S. government sites, including the Census Bureau and the SEC, while insisting none of those incidents counted as breaches.
Now the same company is pitching itself as the internet's night watchman. "Defenders need to have a tighter OODA loop than attackers," Brockman said, borrowing a military term for the cycle of observing, orienting, deciding, and acting, and argued that's possible "especially if defenders have access to stronger models than attackers."
He went further, floating a future where "authorized defenders (such as government)" scan the internet for vulnerable servers and, "in extreme cases," patch them remotely. "It should thus be a national priority to ensure that we always have the most capable cyber models," he said.
To protect the world from the dangers of AI, OpenAI has committed $1 billion in subsidized access to Daybreak, its AI program for defenders protecting critical infrastructure. Brockman said the company is also fixing "several other significant bugs," including a remote code execution flaw that Node.js announced Wednesday.
And PHP won't be the last. “We expect to find many more such issues over upcoming months,” Brockman said. Hopefully the disclosures go smoother next time—ChatGPT could probably help draft the emails.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Elon Musk said Tuesday that SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees of independent directors to study a merger, though no terms have been agreed.
- A combined company worth roughly $3.5 trillion would own the Grok chatbot, X, Starlink, the Terafab chip project, the Starmind orbital data center plan, and Tesla's robotaxi and Optimus businesses.
- Any deal needs the backing of 50% of all outstanding Tesla shares, which Musk called "quite a high hurdle," and Tesla's annual meeting is set for December 3.
Elon Musk said Tuesday that the boards of SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees to study merging his two biggest companies, a deal that would put rockets, electric cars, humanoid robots, a social network and the Grok chatbot inside a single corporation worth roughly $3.5 trillion.
“I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity,” Musk said on SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call. The singularity is Silicon Valley shorthand for the point where AI outsmarts humans and starts improving itself faster than anyone can keep up.
He then listed what the two companies would share: “superintelligence software, chip design, the Terafab obviously, robotics, mass-to-orbit with the Starmind constellation, connectivity.”
In plain English, that means AI models, custom chips, a giant chip factory, robots, and satellites that work as data centers in orbit.
If it happens, one company—with one man holding the majority of its votes—would own a leading AI chatbot, the social network that feeds it data, the satellites that connect it, the factory that makes its chips, and the cars and robots it is meant to drive.
Nothing has been signed and Musk warned that assuming a merger is a certainty “would be overstating it.” If you own an S&P 500 index fund, you already hold a sliver of Tesla—not SpaceX—and in an all-stock deal those shares would likely be swapped for stock in the combined company.
It would be Musk’s third consolidation since March 2025, when xAI absorbed X (formerly Twitter). In February, SpaceX swallowed xAI in a deal valuing the AI company at $250 billion, weeks after Tesla put about $2 billion into it; in June, SpaceX went public in the largest IPO ever.
SpaceX reported third-quarter revenue of $14.58 billion on Tuesday, well above the $12.72 billion analysts expected. It also booked its first quarterly profit since going public, largely by renting the computing power of its AI server farms to firms such as Anthropic and Google.
The most ambitious piece is Starmind, SpaceX’s plan to put AI data centers in orbit. The company has asked U.S. regulators to approve up to 1 million satellites that would run AI models on near-constant sunlight, and Musk expects deployments to start in late 2027 and reach “significant scale” in 2028.
Musk’s argument is that Earth is running out of room and electricity for AI, and the politics back him up. An Annenberg survey found 61% of Americans now oppose new data centers in their area, and roughly $130 billion in projects were blocked or delayed in the first quarter of 2026 alone.
SpaceX’s own IPO paperwork, however, warned investors that orbital AI computing relies on “unproven technologies” and “may not achieve commercial viability.” Tesla’s main contribution would be Terafab, a $16.8 billion chip factory the two companies are building in Texas to supply Optimus robots, Cybercab robotaxis, and those space data centers.
Musk isn't the first to look past dry land to keep servers cool. Microsoft's Project Natick sank 855 servers off the coast of Scotland in 2018. Over two years only six failed, a 0.7% rate against 5.9% for a comparable group on land, yet Microsoft shut the program down anyway, with cloud operations chief Noelle Walsh saying, “I’m not building subsea data centers anywhere in the world.”
China has since picked up the idea with a wind-powered underwater data center about six miles off Shanghai, which its builder, HiCloud, says uses at least 30% less electricity than land-based rivals, while startup Lonestar aimed at launching a small data storage unit toward the Moon in early 2025.
Wall Street mostly likes the idea, at the right price. “We believe this is a no-brainer move for both SpaceX and Tesla, it comes down to the price for shareholders,” Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co. told Reuters, estimating Tesla shares would need to be valued around $550 apiece—a premium, or bonus over the market price, big enough to win the vote.
Tesla spiked almost 4% after Elon’s statements went public. His words were more powerful for Tesla’s stocks than building a flying car, considering the stock dipped after the demonstration.
Even if nothing is for certain, markets are flirting with the idea. Tesla investor Gene Munster of Deepwater Asset Management now puts the odds of a deal within two years at 95%.
SpaceX is also a major contractor for the U.S. military, intelligence agencies, and NASA, while Tesla relies heavily on its Shanghai factory, a national security mix Reuters said could draw scrutiny from both Washington and Beijing.
A merger would also hand Musk the tighter grip on Tesla he has long demanded. He owns about 20% of Tesla but controls most of SpaceX’s votes through supervoting shares—stock that carries extra votes—and Barclays estimates he would hold about 56% of the votes in a combined company.
SpaceX reacted much more favorably with a 10% spike, the best movement since June.
Any deal still needs the support of 50% of all outstanding Tesla shares, not just those cast, a bar Musk called “quite a high hurdle.” Barclays suggested last week that an announcement could come before Tesla’s annual meeting on December 3.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Nate Kostar
items.content:
Cardano Foundation urges EU against expanding MiCA rules to DeFi and staking
The foundation called for regulation based on financial risks rather than technology, warning that overlapping rules could create uncertainty for crypto businesses across the EU.
The Cardano Foundation has urged the European Union not to introduce new, standalone regulations for decentralized finance and staking, arguing that existing financial laws should govern such activities based on their functions and risks rather than the technologies they use.
In a Wednesday blog post outlining its 19-page Sept. 30 submission to the European Commission, the foundation called for a distinction between direct participation in decentralized networks and financial services provided by intermediaries, particularly those involving custody or control of users’ assets.
“Regulation should follow the substance of an activity, the functions performed, and the risks created, not the technology through which it is conducted,” the foundation wrote.
The foundation said Cardano users can delegate their native ADA (ADA) tokens to help secure the network without surrendering custody or locking their tokens, arguing that such participation should be treated differently from staking services operated by intermediaries.
The submission also called for clearer distinctions between the EU’s Markets in Crypto Assets Regulation (MiCA) and existing financial laws, warning that overlapping requirements and inconsistent interpretations across member states could create uncertainty for crypto businesses.
The foundation’s position comes as EU regulators consider expanding oversight of crypto services. In September, the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) recommended additional safeguards for staking, lending and borrowing, along with a new regulated service category for firms providing access to DeFi protocols.
The Cardano Foundation has also pushed for greater regulatory clarity across the Atlantic, joining five other blockchain organizations in an Oct. 20 letter urging the US Securities and Exchange Commission to formally recognize digital commodities as non-securities under its proposed crypto framework.

items.author: Aaron Wise
items.content:
A bug that allows hackers to remotely execute code has been discovered in PHP, the language that powers 70% of the world’s websites.
PHP shipped emergency fixes today for two of the most critical flaws, but over one-third of the web remains unpatched as of publication time.
The language, used to program website backends, runs on servers, not in the browser, and sends its resulting HTML or other dynamic data to the browser.
Official fixed releases only cover PHP 8.2 and newer, leaving over one-third of PHP websites without a patch.
Mid-day, backports were starting to roll out across older versions 7.4-8.1. Unfortunately, according to one estimate, more than 800,000 internet hosts serving content to millions of websites run a branch of PHP so old “that will get no fix” at all.
The two flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are collectively PHP2Shell.
PHP2Shell lets an unauthenticated attacker run code on a web server and serve buggy outputs to a user’s browser.
Hackers’ exploits can occur even before a website’s own code executes.
Read more: Whitehat hacker accuses Injective of ghosting after $500M bug disclosure
AI hacked PHP, found a bug affecting most websites
A security researcher using OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol model discovered the bug during an August audit funded by OpenAI.
That researcher was part of Calif, a partner in OpenAI’s Patch the Planet program, which pairs frontier models with expert human cybersecurity review.
The bug class had been flagged decades earlier yet dismissed as too hard to exploit, Calif’s CEO Thai Duong told the Wall Street Journal.
However, AI hackers have now figured out how to seize control of a server’s memory within a few dozen requests.
Wiz, a division of Google Cloud, confirmed the flaws independently. Wiz’s co-founder called PHP2Shell “the most severe AI vulnerability that was ever found,” and one humans would probably never have found.
Cloudflare reacts as PHP alarms ring around the world
Cloudflare’s CTO Dane Knecht reported live exploit vectors for every customer, including free plans.
The website cacheing giant implemented a stopgap emergency measure overnight before announcing more patches a few hours later.
The PHP bug had worldwide impact. Finland’s state IT center shut several government web services as a precaution.
Meanwhile, in the Netherlands, NotuBiz’s council information sites for local governments went offline, with MijnOverheid and the Dutch parliament’s site following.
Patched versions of PHP include 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. However, 27% of PHP sites still run PHP 7, and 7.7% run PHP 5, which remain unpatched.
GoDaddy urged customers to upgrade.

items.content:
In brief
- Bitcoin trades near $84,500, up 2.5% in 24 hours, as the crypto market cap rose 2.6% to $2.82 trillion; XRP gained 4.1% and Zcash 11.2%.
- Brent crude near $108 and a 5.09% 10-year Treasury yield drove October's selloff, and both eased slightly on Wednesday.
- Bitcoin technical indicators still suggest caution, but prediction markets lean optimistically bullish.
Bitcoin traders and hodlers are breathing this week after a pretty spooky start to the month with the historically best gains.
Bitcoin traded near $84,500 on Wednesday, up 2.5% over 24 hours, as the crypto market bounced back from a mid-October slide that pushed it below $80,000. The total crypto market capitalization, the combined value of every coin, rose 2.2% to $2.9 trillion.
Ethereum climbed 2.5% to $2,504, Solana gained 2.2% to $108.18 and BNB rose 2% to $749. XRP led the large caps with a 4.1% gain to $1.37, while Zcash jumped 11.2% to $1,332 and has now added 15.3% over seven days.
The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, a 0-to-100 gauge where 0 means extreme fear and 100 means extreme greed, reads 55, which counts as neutral but is 3 points ahead of yesterday’s readings. In other words, it seems like traders have stopped panicking, but they are not yet chasing prices.
Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, has swung between $97 and $112 a barrel this month and traded near $108 on Wednesday. The war with Iran keeps supply fears alive, and Washington rejected an Iranian plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in late September.
Oil matters to crypto because it feeds inflation. U.S. consumer prices rose 3.7% in September from a year earlier, above the 3.6% economists expected and up from 3.4% in August. Higher inflation pushes up Treasury yields, the annual return investors demand for lending to the U.S. government. Government bonds paying more than 5% with almost no default risk pull money away from stocks and crypto, and higher rates make the borrowing behind leveraged trades costlier.
The Federal Reserve's benchmark rate sits at 3.75% to 4% after a September hike, and CME FedWatch gives about an eight-in-ten chance of a hold at the Oct. 28 meeting. Markets firmly expect a hike on Dec. 9.
Bitcoin price: Going up, but weak
On the daily chart, Bitcoin opened Wednesday at $82,928.80 and has reached $84,726.28, up 1.94% for the candle, after bouncing about 6% from this month's low near $79,711. Its current price is pressing up, trying to approach the natural resistance at $87,422.70.
Bitcoin’s latest rally ran from $62,763 to a September high of $87,422.70. That trend marked a strong support at $81,603. Bitcoin lost the level in the October dip and has now reclaimed it, with movement still in the upper side of its bounce..
The 50-day exponential moving average, an average of recent closing prices that gives more weight to the most recent days, sits near $80,782, above the 200-day moving average at about $76,084. A 50-day above the 200-day is the standard sign of an uptrend, and Bitcoin trades 4.6% above the shorter average.
The Relative Strength Index, or RSI, which scores recent buying against selling on a 0-to-100 scale, reads 58.5. Readings above 50 mean buyers hold the edge, while 70 marks overbought territory, so momentum is not yet stretched but is moving towards a bullish mood.
The bullish scenario needs a daily close above $84,726, today's high, ideally with ADX—an indicator of a trend’s strength over time—climbing back above 25 to confirm a trend. That would open a natural target at around $86,090, and then the September high at $87,422.70.
Traders on Myriad, a prediction market built by Decrypt's parent company Dastan, put the odds of Bitcoin touching $87,500 in October at 31%, down from 45% on Oct. 12. A $90,000 touch is priced at 18%.
A stall below $84,726 would keep Bitcoin inside the roughly $79,700 to $87,400 range that has held since late September, which fits an ADX under 20.
The bearish case starts with a daily close below $81,603. That would expose the 50-day EMA at $80,782, then the October low near $79,711, and the 200-day EMA at $76,084.

items.content:
UK financial watchdog opens consultations for DeFi guidance, crypto laws
The UK Financial Conduct Authority consultations came just weeks after the agency opened applications for companies under its new crypto regulatory regime.
The UK’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) announced two consultation periods for how companies using decentralized finance can comply with its guidance, and exclusions for certain crypto assets following “recent legislative changes.”
In a Wednesday notice, the FCA opened consultation periods for helping DeFi companies comply with the financial watchdog’s rules on money laundering and financial crime. The agency also announced a consultation for “exclusions from cryptoasset regulation,” citing recent legislation in the country.
Regarding DeFi, the FCA said that the proposed guidance “seeks to clarify existing rules rather than establish new policy.”
“DeFi sits among the most innovative parts of [Financial Services],” said the UK Cryptoasset Business Council in response to the consultations. “The UK can still strike the right balance - clear perimeter rules, expectations that stay proportionate, and a framework that lets responsible innovation take root here instead of migrating elsewhere [...] the FCA needs to get this right.”
The crypto regulation exclusions referred to the FCA’s reveal of a regulatory regime, including stablecoin holding arrangements and reserve assets, expected to be enforced starting in October 2027. The FCA opened applications for crypto entities on Sept. 30, with a Feb. 28, 2027 deadline for companies seeking to be in compliance with the rules.
Related: UK sanctions three crypto exchanges tied to Russian illicit funds
